mainEntity.name: How much does a Peugeot 3008 Hybrid powertrain replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt Peugeot 3008 Hybrid powertrain typically costs £2,800-£5,500 supply-only, depending on the system and supplier. Hybrid4 diesel-electric units range £2,800-£4,500, while Plug-in Hybrid petrol-electric units range £3,200-£5,500. Used units start from £1,800. Supply & fit adds £800-£1,500 labour due to high-voltage system complexity. Main dealer replacement can exceed £8,000-£10,000.

mainEntity.name: What are the most common Peugeot 3008 Hybrid problems?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common Peugeot 3008 Hybrid problems are high-voltage battery degradation reducing electric range, electric motor bearing wear causing noise, power inverter failure triggering system shutdown, and engine-specific issues - EGR/DPF on the Hybrid4 diesel or HPFP/timing chain on the PHEV petrol. Both systems are complex and require specialist diagnostics.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the hybrid powertrain on a Peugeot 3008?

acceptedAnswer.text: Replacing a Peugeot 3008 Hybrid powertrain is worthwhile if the vehicle is otherwise sound. A rebuilt unit costs £2,800-£5,500 versus £10,000-£30,000 for a comparable used hybrid 3008. With dealer replacement potentially exceeding £8,000-£10,000, specialist rebuilt units offer significant savings. Hybrid vehicles command strong residuals, making replacement a sensible investment.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Peugeot 3008 Hybrid battery last?

acceptedAnswer.text: With proper maintenance, the Peugeot 3008 Hybrid battery typically lasts 8-10 years or 80,000-120,000 miles. The Hybrid4's smaller 1.1 kWh battery is more sensitive to degradation than the PHEV's 13.2 kWh pack. Battery health checks should be performed regularly. If you notice reduced electric-only range, have the battery inspected promptly.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between Hybrid4 and Plug-in Hybrid?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Hybrid4 (2012-2016) is a diesel-electric hybrid with a 2.0L DW10BTED4 diesel engine, a rear-mounted electric motor (37hp) and a 1.1 kWh battery. It is self-charging (no plug-in) and offers low-speed electric-only driving with all-wheel drive capability. The Plug-in Hybrid (2020-2024) is a petrol-electric hybrid with a 1.6L EP6FDT turbo petrol engine, a front-mounted electric motor (113hp) and a 13.2 kWh battery. It can be plugged in for charging and offers extended electric-only range.

mainEntity.name: How do I find my Peugeot 3008 Hybrid powertrain code?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your Peugeot 3008 Hybrid powertrain code is DW10BTED4+Electric for Hybrid4 models (2012-2016) or EP6FDT+Electric for Plug-in Hybrid models (2020-2024). It appears on the VIN plate under the bonnet, on the engine block, or on your V5C registration document section D.2. Enter your reg above for instant verification.

historyTimeline.h2: Peugeot 3008 Hybrid4 & Plug-in Hybrid - Powertrain History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Peugeot 3008 Hybrid represents two distinct electrified powertrains across the model's history. The first-generation Hybrid4 (2012-2016) combined a 2.0-litre DW10BTED4 diesel engine with a rear electric motor for all-wheel drive capability, delivering 200hp combined and electric-only low-speed driving. The second-generation Plug-in Hybrid (2020-2024) paired a 1.6-litre EP6FDT turbo petrol engine with a more powerful front-mounted electric motor, offering up to 300hp combined and extended electric-only range. Both systems recover energy via regenerative braking - but the PHEV can be plugged in for battery charging, while the Hybrid4 is self-charging. Replacement of these complex hybrid powertrains requires specialist knowledge of high-voltage systems and inverter calibration.

milestones.description: **2012** - Hybrid4 (DW10BTED4+Electric) launched as world's first diesel-electric hybrid SUV, producing 200hp combined
**2020** - Plug-in Hybrid (EP6FDT+Electric) launched with second-generation 3008, producing 225-300hp combined
**2021** - Updated PHEV battery capacity and electric motor calibration for improved electric-only range
**2022** - PHEV carries over with minor infotainment updates
**2024** - Production continues with PHEV as the primary electrified option

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every DW10BTED4+Electric and EP6FDT+Electric powertrain fitted to the Peugeot 3008 Hybrid is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Peugeot 3008 Hybrid Powertrain Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Peugeot 3008 Hybrid is a complex, advanced powertrain - combining internal combustion engines with electric motors, high-voltage batteries and sophisticated control systems. The Hybrid4's diesel-electric system and the Plug-in Hybrid's petrol-electric architecture each have distinct failure patterns. Hybrid battery degradation, inverter faults and electric motor bearing wear are the primary drivers of replacement enquiries. Every rebuilt Peugeot 3008 Hybrid powertrain through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty - with specialist high-voltage system integration and calibration included.

problems.h4: Hybrid Battery Degradation - Why Peugeot 3008 Hybrid Powertrains Lose Electric Range
problems.rootCause: High-voltage battery cells degrade over time, reducing capacity and electric-only range. The Hybrid4's 1.1 kWh battery is particularly susceptible to capacity loss in hot climates. The PHEV's 13.2 kWh battery can also lose capacity, affecting electric-only range and overall fuel economy. Battery management system (BMS) faults can also trigger system warnings and reduced power output.

repairOptions.tier: Intermediate - Battery Cell Replacement / BMS Reset
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of degraded battery cells, BMS recalibration, system health check
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early; extends battery life by 20k-40k miles

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt unit with new battery pack, electric motor and inverter, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if battery degradation has affected inverter or motor health

problems.recommendation: Hybrid battery degradation is the most common failure on both Hybrid4 and PHEV systems. If you notice reduced electric-only range, have the battery health checked immediately. The Hybrid4's smaller battery is more sensitive to degradation than the PHEV's larger pack. If the battery has lost more than 30% of its capacity, a replacement is usually more cost-effective than continued use. A rebuilt hybrid powertrain with a new battery pack is the most reliable long-term solution.
problems.cta: -> Enquire about Peugeot 3008 Hybrid battery and powertrain replacement

problems.h4: Electric Motor & Inverter Failure - Why Peugeot 3008 Hybrid Systems Lose Power
problems.rootCause: The electric motor's bearings can wear over time, causing noise and vibration. The power inverter - which converts DC battery power to AC motor power - can fail due to thermal stress or coolant leaks. The Hybrid4's rear-mounted motor is particularly susceptible to bearing wear due to its exposed location. The PHEV's front-mounted motor is better protected but shares inverter vulnerability.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of electric motor or inverter, cooling system flush, system recalibration
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if engine and battery are healthy

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt unit with new motor, inverter, battery and engine components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if motor/inverter failure has caused system-wide damage

problems.recommendation: Electric motor and inverter failures on the Peugeot 3008 Hybrid are less common than battery degradation but can be catastrophic. If you hear unusual whining or buzzing noises, have the system inspected immediately. Replacing the motor or inverter in isolation is effective if the battery and engine are healthy. If the failure has caused electrical system damage, a complete rebuilt hybrid powertrain is the safest option. The Hybrid4's rear motor is more exposed to road debris - consider protective measures.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt Peugeot 3008 Hybrid powertrain prices

problems.h4: Diesel Engine Failure (Hybrid4) - Why DW10BTED4 Units Fail
problems.rootCause: The Hybrid4's diesel engine shares the same vulnerabilities as the standard DW10BTED4 - EGR cooler failure, DPF blockage and injector seal wear. The hybrid system's stop-start nature can place additional stress on the engine, as frequent engine cycling accelerates wear on the turbocharger and EGR system.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: EGR cooler replacement, DPF clean, injector seal replacement
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught before engine damage occurs

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt unit with new diesel engine, electric motor and battery, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if engine damage has occurred or hybrid system integration is compromised

problems.recommendation: The Hybrid4's diesel engine is generally robust when maintained, but the hybrid system's stop-start nature can accelerate wear. If you notice loss of power, blue smoke or coolant loss, have the engine inspected immediately. A rebuilt Hybrid4 powertrain with upgraded diesel engine components and a fresh battery pack offers the best long-term reliability.

problems.h4: Petrol Engine Failure (PHEV) - Why EP6FDT Units Fail
problems.rootCause: The PHEV's EP6FDT petrol engine shares vulnerabilities with the standard 1.6 THP - high-pressure fuel pump failure, timing chain guide wear and carbon buildup. The PHEV system's electric-only driving means the petrol engine can be cold-started less frequently, potentially leading to oil dilution and carbon buildup.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: HPFP replacement, timing chain kit, carbon cleaning
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught before engine damage occurs

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt unit with new petrol engine, electric motor and battery, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if engine damage has occurred or hybrid system integration is compromised

problems.recommendation: The PHEV's petrol engine is generally robust but the HPFP and timing chain should be inspected at 60,000 miles. If you notice hard starting, misfires or cold-start rattle, address it immediately. A rebuilt PHEV powertrain with upgraded engine components and a fresh battery pack offers the best long-term reliability.
